Following the transfer of production to Luthien Armor Works, the Cizin entered standard DCMS service and has been distributed across multiple regiments engaged in operations against the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, where its speed remains valued in mobile warfare across varied terrain.

The Support variant was developed in 3124 to extend the Cizin's operational reach and provide long-range fire coverage for fast-attack formations. Where the standard Cizin closes range aggressively, the Support variant holds at distance, its turreted extended-range large laser linked to the targeting computer for precision engagement at range. A front-mounted Streak LRM-15 provides sustained indirect fire capability, and the sixteen volleys of ammunition carried supports extended independent operations. The addition of an ECM suite distinguishes the Support variant as an electronic warfare platform as much as a fire support asset, disrupting enemy targeting telemetry in ways the standard variant cannot.

The Galedon Regulars have employed the Support variant as a force multiplier in combined lance operations against AFFS forces, using its ECM capability to suppress precision targeting systems. During the conquest of McGhee, a Support variant crew discovered an AFFS recon lance from the Fourth Robinson Rangers and disrupted their communications long enough to allow Combine forces to outmaneuver the defenders and capture Clatterbuck City the following day.

The standardized full-production model of the Cobra Transport VTOL, entering SLDF service in 2620. The standard configuration carries cargo and personnel across a range of mission profiles and represents the most widely produced Cobra variant. Active through the Star League era, the standard model formed the backbone of SLDF tactical logistics flights and was issued to line formations across all military regions. Following the reactivation of the Aldis Industries production line, the standard configuration resumed production for Republic of the Sphere logistics units.

The Command configuration adapts the standard Cobra Transport VTOL with enhanced communications equipment and command staff accommodations, trading a portion of internal cargo space for improved command and control capability. Introduced in 2622, the Command variant serves as a mobile operations center for battalion and regimental-level commanders requiring airborne coordination during active engagements. The configuration includes additional communications consoles and a small planning space for staff officers to manage ongoing operations from overhead positions.

The MASH configuration converts the Cobra's internal hold into a mobile surgical and patient care facility, equipped to handle emergency trauma cases at or near the forward edge of battle. Introduced in 2669, the MASH variant provides medical units with a capable airmobile surgical platform that can operate independently of ground-based field hospitals when forward facilities are unavailable or overwhelmed. The configuration includes surgical stations, recovery berths, and medical supply storage, enabling sustained casualty treatment during extended operations.

The prototype and initial evaluation configuration, completing testing and assessment by Aldis Industries and SLDF evaluators from 2582. The (Original) configuration established the structural and systems baseline for subsequent production variants and saw only limited operational deployment, serving primarily to validate the design's performance envelope and identify areas requiring refinement before full-rate production. Most (Original) examples were either upgraded to production standard or retained by Aldis as engineering reference vehicles.

The standard fusion-powered Command Van is the most common command vehicle in the Inner Sphere, found in service with every major military and most planetary militias. Its ubiquity means that any combined-arms formation, no matter how modest, can obtain at least a basic level of battlefield coordination. Variants differ primarily in the quality of their internal electronics, which ranges from cutting-edge Star League salvage to barely functional jury-rigged systems.

The ICE-powered Command Van appeared during the worst years of the Succession Wars, when fusion engines were stripped from support vehicles to keep BattleMechs operational. These downgraded variants require power amplifiers to operate their communications equipment and laser armament. They remain in service with militia formations and peripheral states where fusion engines remain scarce or where the additional maintenance overhead of a fusion plant is not justified by the command van's limited combat role.

The Q-Vehicle is a deceptive field refit that disguises the Command Van as a civilian transport. Commanders remove obvious military markings and conceal weapons behind false panels, creating a vehicle that can infiltrate areas where a military presence would draw unwanted attention. Q-Vehicles are most commonly found in the periphery and among irregular forces, where they serve as ambush platforms against overconfident raiders. The conversion is simple enough that virtually any field workshop can perform it.

An experimental Capellan Confederation modification from the early thirty-first century, the Fission variant replaced the Jones combustion engine with a fission power plant, freeing weight for a third medium laser and additional protection including sponson-mounted flamers and machine guns. The concept proved unworkable in sustained operations: fission engines of the era could not match combustion equivalents in combat reliability, and replacement components were chronically unavailable. Surviving examples served briefly in CCAF secondary commands before disappearing from active inventories within a generation.

Optimized for urban warfare and anti-infantry operations, the Flamer variant adds vehicular flamers fore and aft with ammunition reserves, alongside additional machine guns and three medium lasers in the turret. The heavily infantry-focused configuration stands as a specialized role assignment rather than a general replacement for the standard model, deployed by units expecting dense urban combat or needing to defend against mass infantry assaults in close terrain.

Red Devil's early thirty-first century experiment with a fusion-powered Condor produced a modest run before the Clan Invasion disrupted Pandora. The fusion engine enabled an AC/10 with ample ammunition and an additional medium laser, trading the standard ICE configuration for greater firepower at the cost of a higher manufacturing price. Surviving examples became increasingly rare after the fall of Pandora, and the variant is now encountered primarily in older reserve formations and on the salvage market.

The most recent Panpour production variant, the LAC replaces the standard weapons suite with a Light Autocannon/5, paired medium re-engineered lasers, and an anti-missile system. The design philosophy reflects lessons from the ilClan era, emphasizing defensive capability and ammunition efficiency over peak offensive output. Entering service in the 3140s, the LAC sees use in Federated Suns secondary commands and allied formations valuing logistical sustainability in contested resupply environments.

A Dark Age production variant from Jalastar's Panpour facility, the Laser Upgrade equips the Condor hull with three medium re-engineered lasers and ferro-fibrous armor, using a fusion engine rather than the original combustion plant. The energy-only weapons configuration eliminates ammunition dependency entirely, a significant advantage in the fragmented logistics environment of the post-Jihad and Dark Age periods. The variant sees adoption primarily in Republic-adjacent Federated Suns commands and independent systems along the former FedCom border.

A hybrid configuration bridging the standard Condor and the later Upgrade, the Laser variant uses a standard fusion engine to power four extended-range medium lasers and three SRM-2 launchers in the turret. Produced at both Pandora and Panpour, this variant was most active during the Clan Invasion and Civil War eras, valued by units requiring sustained energy firepower without dependence on the autocannon ammunition that logistics-strained commands often struggled to supply.

CCAF technicians favored an all-energy weapons configuration that eliminated ammunition dependence, stripping the GM Whirlwind autocannon and replacing it with two additional medium lasers for a total of four. The modification reflects Capellan logistical doctrine prioritizing sustainability over peak firepower, and the Liao variant remained a fixture of House Liao hover cavalry formations through the Succession Wars and beyond.

components.armor: Bowie Glinting Blade Reflective with CASE

text.deployment: Introduced during the Dark Age following the Lyran Alliance's recapture of Pandora in 3110, the Ultra variant is a significant capability upgrade, combining an ultra autocannon, medium chemical lasers, reflective armor, an anti-missile system, and a TAG designator in a hull faster than the original Condor's best speed. Intended to give Lyran armored cavalry a qualitative edge over opponents fielding conventional armor, the Ultra sees primary use in Lyran front-line hover regiments where its combined-arms suite makes it valuable in high-intensity operations.

Quikscell's extensive modernization of the Condor platform produced a vehicle sharing only its name and general role with the original Red Devil design. The XL fusion engine, LRM-15 launcher, and LB-X autocannon combination created a tank capable of engaging targets at ranges the original Condor could not reach, while ferro-fibrous armor improved survivability. Demand consistently outpaced Richvale production capacity, prompting Quikscell to sell unassembled kit variants to operators who could not wait for completed vehicles. The Upgrade served across the Lyran Commonwealth, mercenary commands, and former Federated Commonwealth forces throughout the Jihad era and into the Dark Age.

Quikscell's energy-weapon alternative to the standard Upgrade replaces the LB-X autocannon with a Cyclops extended-range large laser, adding an anti-missile system and Guardian ECM suite at the cost of one ton of armor compared to the baseline Upgrade. The variant sacrifices some raw firepower for operational independence from ammunition supply, a priority in the isolated supply chains of the Jihad era. The ECM protection also makes it difficult for missile-heavy opponents to achieve lock-on at range. Deployed primarily in Lyran Commonwealth and allied commands, the Laser version sees wider adoption in garrison forces and secondary commands where ammunition resupply is uncertain.

Produced at Pandora under Clan Jade Falcon's oversight at the direction of Merchant Factor Daniel, the C variant incorporates Clan weapon technology including two ProtoMech autocannons and three medium chemical lasers into the Condor hull. Intended for local Jade Falcon use with the possibility of Inner Sphere export sales, the economics of the production line proved marginal and output remained limited. The variant has since fallen out of production, and examples in Inner Sphere service are uncommon.

text.overview: Honestly, this would be a nice, cheap variant for the classic Condor hovertank. It cuts out all the excesses like lasers, heat sinks, and power amplifiers in favor of a more powerful engine that gives it a serious boost in speed, as well as a few extra tons of armor. It's just unfortunate that the techs also cut corners when it came to intuitive control systems and, apparently, effective braking systems.

text.deployment: The standard Condor MPT serves Republic of the Sphere Standing Guard formations as the primary medium tank, conducting patrols, supporting police actions, and providing a mobile fire base for militia commands. In front-line Brigades it fills a cavalry role, using its speed to flank opponents and disrupt formations alongside heavier assets. The standard armor version is increasingly rare in active combat commands, as field reactive armor upgrades have become nearly universal in units expecting sustained enemy contact.

The reactive armor refit of the Condor MPT began informally as a field modification among front-line Republic Brigades, sourcing reactive plating through Aldis while simultaneously upgrading the Kinnol MBT with the same treatment. The modification's widespread adoption prompted the DR&R to consider incorporating it into new production orders, effectively formalizing what had become a de facto standard configuration for combat-deployed MPTs. Operationally identical to the standard model beyond the improved protection, the Reactive variant has become the expected front-line configuration.

text.overview: Hover variants of the Coolant Truck extend the concept of battlefield thermal support to operational environments where wheeled vehicles face terrain limitations. Appearing across the Inner Sphere in response to broader demand for mobile heat management support, hover coolant trucks serve formations operating in terrain that wheeled designs cannot reliably cross, including wetlands, river obstacles, and broken ground. They share the same fundamental mission profile as the wheeled 135-K: providing emergency cooling support to BattleMechs in the field, allowing formations to sustain combat effectiveness in conditions that would otherwise force overheated units to withdraw. Most variants within the hover configuration differ from one another primarily in the type of coolant carried, typically selected to match the heat sink fluid used by friendly 'Mechs in the formation.
text.capabilities: Hover variants of the Coolant Truck maintain the same core operational systems as the wheeled 135-K, including pressurized cryogenic coolant tanks, multi-point hose connections for BattleMech thermal interfaces, and stirring motors to prevent dangerous temperature gradients in stored coolant. The hover propulsion system trades the wheeled configuration's structural durability and payload stability for improved cross-terrain mobility, allowing cooler teams to reposition across water obstacles, soft ground, and terrain irregularities that would halt wheeled vehicles. This increased positional flexibility comes with added mechanical complexity and maintenance demands compared to ground-contact drive systems. The standard six-person crew configuration is retained, with the familiar division between driver, gunner, and hose-management personnel. As with the wider Coolant Truck family, most distinctions between individual hover configurations relate to coolant selection rather than fundamental structural differences.
text.deployment: Hover coolant trucks serve the same support echelon role as the wheeled 135-K, operating under Master Tech command within a regiment's maintenance contingent. The hover configuration is particularly suited to formations operating in wetland, mountainous, or otherwise broken terrain environments where wheeled vehicles cannot reliably follow combat elements. The mobility advantage allows hover crews to reposition more rapidly in response to shifting battle lines, though the increased mechanical demands of hover propulsion require additional maintenance attention. Deployment doctrine otherwise mirrors the standard Coolant Truck pattern: stage at distance from the active engagement, service overheated 'Mechs cycling back from the front, and avoid direct contact with combat units when possible.
text.battleHistory: Hover variants of the Coolant Truck first appeared in 2602 as the Star League's military technology continued to mature and demand for terrain-capable thermal support vehicles grew beyond what wheeled designs could address. The hover configuration extended the Coolant Truck concept to the full range of operational environments encountered by Inner Sphere military forces, from river deltas and wetlands to rocky highland terrain where wheeled support vehicles struggled to maintain formation contact. No single manufacturer is recorded as the originator of the hover configuration, and production developed across multiple Inner Sphere factions as local operational requirements drove independent adoption. Through the Succession Wars, hover coolant trucks served wherever BattleMech formations required thermal support in conditions that demanded cross-terrain mobility from their support echelons, filling the same critical function the wheeled 135-K provided in more permissive environments.

text.overview: Tracked variants of the Coolant Truck extend battlefield thermal support capability to heavy terrain environments, providing the same fundamental service as the wheeled 135-K in conditions where tracked drive systems outperform wheeled configurations. Appearing across the Inner Sphere beyond the Draconis Combine's wheeled production, tracked coolant trucks serve formations operating in mud, rubble, loose soil, and other difficult surfaces. They carry cryogenic coolant supplies for interfacing with overheated BattleMechs and share the same general mission doctrine as the rest of the Coolant Truck family. Most tracked variants differ from one another primarily in the coolant compounds they carry rather than in major mechanical differences, with selection driven by the heat sink fluid used in the BattleMechs they support.
text.capabilities: Tracked coolant truck variants share the core operational systems of the wheeled 135-K, including armored cryogenic tanks, multi-point BattleMech cooling interfaces, and the stirring motors that prevent dangerous temperature gradients in stored coolant. The tracked drive system provides superior traction on soft, wet, or loose terrain compared to wheeled configurations, maintaining useful mobility in conditions that would bog down conventional wheeled support vehicles. This enhanced terrain capability comes with reduced top speed relative to wheeled equivalents and increased mechanical complexity in the drive system. The standard six-person crew configuration is retained, with driver, gunner, and hose-management personnel fulfilling the same roles as in other Coolant Truck variants. Specific armament and coolant system details vary by individual configuration and manufacturer.
text.deployment: Tracked coolant trucks serve the standard support echelon role under Master Tech command, deploying at distance from active engagements to service overheating BattleMechs. The tracked configuration is specifically suited to deployments in marsh, agricultural, rubble-strewn urban, or winter terrain, where wheeled designs lose mobility and hover variants risk mechanical damage from debris ingestion. Formation commanders operating in such environments frequently specify tracked coolers over wheeled or hover equivalents when requisitioning support assets. Deployment doctrine otherwise follows the standard Coolant Truck pattern, with regimental battle groups fielding approximately six coolers and crews following standard procedures for BattleMech hook-up and coolant delivery.
text.battleHistory: Tracked variants of the Coolant Truck developed within the Star League period, first appearing in 2592 as the original wheeled 135-K's terrain limitations became apparent in a wider range of operational environments. The tracked configuration extended coolant truck support to formations operating in conditions that compromised wheeled vehicle performance, filling a gap in support echelon capability for units assigned to difficult terrain zones. No single manufacturer is associated with the tracked variant, and production developed independently across multiple Inner Sphere factions as local operational requirements drove adoption. Through the Succession Wars, tracked coolant trucks served wherever BattleMech formations required reliable thermal support in terrain demanding tracked mobility from support elements, filling the same critical function that the wheeled 135-K provided in more forgiving environments.

text.overview: The Coolant Truck serves as a battlefield support solution born from a fundamental challenge of early BattleMech warfare: managing the extraordinary heat generated by sustained weapons fire. Built by Buda Imperial Vehicles at their facility in the Buda district of Luthien, the 135-K entered Draconis Combine service in 2583 and saw immediate employment during the Siege of Cerberus in the Outworlds Alliance. Codenamed "The Lifesaver" by the crews who depended on it, the vehicle carries armored cryogenic tanks of liquid nitrogen and liquid oxygen, allowing it to rapidly cool overheating BattleMechs in the midst of combat. While a well-maintained BattleMech of modern design might never require such assistance, the 135-K proved indispensable across centuries of warfare against aging machines with compromised cooling systems.
text.capabilities:
The 135-K is a 30-ton wheeled vehicle powered by a Tamia 100 internal combustion engine, achieving a cruising speed of 43 kilometers per hour and a maximum of 64. Its primary systems consist of armored cryogenic tanks carrying five tons of liquid nitrogen and two tons of liquid oxygen, with stirring motors cycling continuously to prevent dangerous temperature gradients from forming in the stored coolant. Five reinforced receptacles connect to long attachment hoses designed to interface with BattleMech cooling systems. The first four receptacles dispense liquid nitrogen for direct thermal management, while the fifth carries liquid oxygen that can supplement a heat-distressed 'Mech's cooling fluid or enrich the fuel for the vehicle's weapons.

The 135-K mounts two turret-mounted Dragon's Breath flamers as self-defense armament, which can also discharge liquid nitrogen when approaching a 'Mech requiring emergency cooling. StarSlab/3 armor provides basic crew protection. Light and medium BattleMechs require a single hook-up point to receive full cooling benefit, while heavier designs need two connections simultaneously, limiting the truck's ability to service multiple large units at once. The Sipher CommSys 1 and Matabushi Sentinel targeting provide battlefield situational awareness appropriate for a support vehicle, and the crew's prize value to enemy forces makes the communications fit an important secondary asset.
text.deployment: Coolant Trucks operate as part of the maintenance and support echelon, falling under the command of a formation's Master Tech. A single well-maintained regimental battle group typically fields about six coolers, deploying them to follow an advance at cautious distance or to stage behind a defensive line where they can service units cycling back from engagement. Each 135-K is crewed by six personnel: a driver, a gunner managing the flamer armament, and four hose-men who handle the cooling connections. Assignment to a cooler crew carries little prestige among combat personnel, though experienced teams develop real pride in their work. Intact coolant truck teams are prized as battlefield captures, and mercenary formations place particular value on seasoned cooler crews, sometimes offering them a share of unit earnings equal to what two Techs would earn to retain their services.
text.battleHistory:
The Coolant Truck originated as a tactical stopgap during the Star League's Reunification War, when early-generation BattleMechs with severe heat management deficiencies were pressed into sustained combat. Archival footage from the period shows ranks of 'Mechs firing full weapons volleys while support trucks sprayed them down continuously, a coordination method that would have appeared extraordinary to crews of later eras. A BattleCorps review of the original TRO:3039 entry corrected two historical details. First, Buda is a district within Luthien rather than a separate planet, with the revised edition removing the ambiguous reference. Second, the Siege of Cerberus took place in 2583, not 2588 as originally printed.

Cerberus, a desert world in the Outworlds Alliance, was among the first major deployments of organized coolant truck support, where SLDF 'Mechs maintaining sustained fire rates overwhelmed Periphery defensive positions. The Outworlds Alliance formally surrendered two years later in 2585. The technological regression of the Succession Wars reshaped the Coolant Truck's role dramatically. Centuries-old BattleMechs staggering into battle with ruptured heat sinks and damaged engine shielding depended on truck support to remain combat effective, and the informal "Lifesaver" designation became literal. A battlefield convention emerged during this period: enemy forces generally extended informal courtesy to 'Mechs connected to a cooler, refraining from targeting them until the connection was broken and the unit moved clear. This convention showed signs of eroding as the Succession Wars deepened.

The recovery of the Helm Memory Core and subsequent technological renaissance gradually reduced dependency on coolant truck support as BattleMech maintenance standards improved. Rebuilt and new designs incorporated effective heat dissipation, reducing the 135-K's role from critical lifeline to specialized support asset. Buda Imperial Vehicles continued production at Luthien through the Civil War era before the line ceased active output.
