text.overview: The Crane Heavy Transport entered service in 3130, barely two years before the HPG Blackout transformed the political theater of the Inner Sphere. Michaelson Heavy Industries designed the vehicle for broad commercial appeal, anticipating growing demand for reliable VTOL-mobile logistics in an era of expanding airmobile doctrine. That calculation proved accurate almost immediately. Procurement inquiries arrived from every major Successor State, and many planetary governments placed independent orders alongside their respective national militaries. The combination of genuine cargo and troop lift capacity with armor protection well above what most dedicated transport platforms offer set the Crane apart in a crowded market. By the time the Blackout disrupted conventional communications and supply chains, the Crane was already embedded in logistics networks across dozens of worlds, positioned to serve whatever factions emerged from the resulting chaos.
text.capabilities:
A Hermes 100 Fusion power plant drives the Crane to a cruising speed of 86 kilometers per hour with a maximum of 129, giving it performance suitable for both rapid insertion and sustained logistics runs across a theater of operations. The hull mounts StarSlab/3 armor in substantial quantity, providing protection considerably greater than most VTOL transports of comparable weight can achieve. This durability is central to the design philosophy: the Crane is built to operate in contested airspace and to survive incidental fire during troop deliveries rather than relying entirely on escort assets.

Combat armament consists of four Scattergun Machine Guns, a deliberately modest package suited to suppressing infantry and deterring light vehicles. The loadout offers no meaningful defense against dedicated gunships or armored opponents, and crews operating in high-threat environments depend on fighter or attack helicopter escorts for protection against serious threats. The Crane's genuine tactical value lies in its cargo capacity and operational flexibility. Airmobile formations use a single Crane to deliver infantry in the opening phase of an operation and then return with ammunition, medical supplies, or replacement personnel, reducing the need for dedicated resupply aircraft. The Garret T10-B communications system and Garret E2b targeting suite provide reliable electronics matched to the vehicle's transport mission profile. When pressed into a direct combat role the design is exposed, and experienced crews know to prioritize evasion and terrain masking over engagement.
text.deployment: The Crane's wide distribution and commercial availability make it a practical choice for nearly any armed force operating in the Dark Age period. Airmobile formations across the Inner Sphere prize it as a combined insertion and logistics platform, relying on a single vehicle type to deliver infantry in the opening phase of an operation before returning with resupply rather than committing dedicated cargo aircraft. Planetary militia forces, private security contractors, and commercial freight operators have adopted the type in comparable numbers. The vehicle's unremarkable profile on civilian flight lines is an operational asset in its own right, allowing intelligence elements to pre-position Cranes on contested worlds without attracting immediate scrutiny. Many vehicles assigned to monitoring missions were deliberately left behind when those missions concluded, absorbed into occupying forces or transferred to local civilian organizations rather than risk exposing their provenance through an extraction attempt.
text.battleHistory:
Michaelson Heavy Industries began production of the Crane at their June facility in 3130, with plants on Ruchbah and Terra added shortly thereafter to meet anticipated cross-faction demand. The timing proved consequential. When the Gray Monday HPG Blackout in 3132 fractured Republic of the Sphere communications and triggered the collapse of prefecture governance across much of the Inner Sphere, the Crane was already in service across dozens of worlds. Its straightforward logistics role made it useful to almost any faction: occupation forces employed it for troop movement, relief organizations requisitioned it for humanitarian aid, and intelligence services valued its unremarkable appearance on crowded flight lines.

In 3139, a Periphery pirate raid on the Federated Suns world of Basantapur destroyed a major hydroelectric facility and left tens of thousands of civilians without power. A relief contingent assembled rapidly from nearby assets, with more than a dozen Cranes flying around-the-clock shifts delivering food, water, medical supplies, and security personnel to affected communities. The operation ran for weeks and demonstrated the practical utility of positioning heavy transport VTOLs on worlds with accessible production infrastructure, a lesson that informed Republic logistics planning throughout the occupation period.

Republic of the Sphere intelligence operations during the turbulent 3140s employed Cranes in a more morally ambiguous capacity. On Milton, following its absorption by the Wolf Empire, RAF assets coordinated with locally embedded Cranes for a covert strike against a Watch facility being rebuilt from a Succession Wars-era bunker. Two Cranes delivered assault teams who successfully destroyed the installation, and captured Clan battle armor was left at the site as a deliberate intelligence plant implicating the Free Worlds League Military. The misdirection briefly complicated Wolf-League relations and typified the quiet, indirect work the Crane performed for Republic intelligence elements throughout the occupation period. The design's greatest strategic asset proved to be exactly what its designers had intended from the outset: it looked like a transport, because it was one.

text.overview: The Crow Scout Helicopter is a military conversion of the Soar search-and-rescue airframe, built by Yan Manufacturing, a civilian aircraft subsidiary of Luthien Armor Works. Developed to restore the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery's diminished airborne electronic intelligence and radio frequency suppression capability, the design retains the proven structural heritage of its civilian predecessor while incorporating a larger powerplant, advanced military electronics, and composite rotor reinforcement meeting combat specifications. The result is one of the fastest combat VTOLs in active production, combining exceptional speed with a capable reconnaissance and electronic warfare suite. First entering service in 3068, the Crow has since established itself as the DCMS's premier airborne scout platform and generated consistent demand from mercenary commands through a separately developed export configuration.
text.capabilities:
With a top speed exceeding 215 kilometers per hour, the Crow is one of the fastest combat vertical takeoff and landing aircraft in production, outpacing the Yellow Jacket and matching the Hawk Moth's engagement range. The DAV 100 fusion engine provides the output necessary to sustain this performance in a military-specification airframe. Two Exostar extended-range small lasers provide a respectable engagement range for a vehicle of its size, though the design is not intended as a primary combatant. Its greatest tactical asset is an extensive electronics package: the Scuti Dualcom communications system integrates an Apple-Churchill Guardian ECM suite for electronic suppression, while the Skyhunter IV targeting system incorporates a Forward-1 TAG designator for guided munitions support and a Wunderland Beagle Active Probe for target acquisition.

Advanced composites reinforce the Crow's rotors to military armor equivalent standards, preserving the flexibility and fatigue tolerance necessary for sustained VTOL operation under combat stress. This construction carries a significant logistical liability, however. All rotor blades are manufactured exclusively at Yan's New Samarkand facility, leaving operators outside the Combine to source locally made substitutes when worn components require replacement. Locally manufactured blades consistently fail at lower stress thresholds than the originals, a problem that grows most apparent when crews push the aircraft to the limits at which Combine pilots typically train. The Crow's armor is intentionally light, accepting vulnerability in direct combat in exchange for the speed that remains its primary survivability mechanism against modern opponents.
text.deployment: Production went primarily to the DCMS under the terms of the Yan arrangement, with early deliveries concentrated in elite units including the Genyosha and the Ryuken regiments before extending to regular line formations. The separately developed export configuration attracted consistent demand from mercenary commands throughout the Inner Sphere, where its substantially lower cost made the design accessible to smaller organizations. By the time standard Crow production reached units in quantity, demand for the following three production runs was already committed, demonstrating the aircraft's broad commercial appeal across both the Combine market and the wider mercenary economy.
text.battleHistory:
The Crow's development began in the aftermath of the Ghost Bear Dominion War, during which the DCMS sustained severe attrition in its light BattleMech forces. The losses stripped the Combine of much of its airborne electronic intelligence and radio frequency suppression coverage, creating a capability gap that Yan Manufacturing's engineers addressed by converting their existing Soar search-and-rescue airframe to military specification. The Soar had established a reputation as one of the most effective civilian rescue platforms in operation, and the design team preserved that reliability as a foundation while integrating a larger engine and military-grade electronics.

Despite the Crow's strong performance profile, the high cost of its premium electronics package made DCMS procurement officers reluctant to commit resources from a still-fragile military budget. The Word of Blake's attack on Luthien changed the calculation, leaving Yan's parent company in financial difficulty and creating conditions for a direct negotiation with Warlord Minamoto's staff. Under the resulting arrangement, the DCMS would receive eighty percent of all Crow production without charge, with the remaining aircraft sold commercially to generate revenue necessary to keep Luthien Armor Works operational. The Warlord's tacit support, conveyed through his conspicuous non-participation in the negotiations, provided the institutional backing needed to proceed, and the first production aircraft entered service within six months of the agreement.

The Jihad's disruption of interstellar travel and communications introduced a persistent complication for non-Combine operators, limiting Yan's ability to ship rotor blade supply packages to units stationed outside the Combine. The company publicly committed to resolving the situation, but the pace of Jihad disruptions repeatedly delayed meaningful progress. Demand for the next three production runs had been fully committed before the aircraft entered general circulation.

text.overview: The aircraft designated Dragonfly was the first Crow Scout Helicopter assigned to the Genyosha, entering DCMS service in 3070 with one of the Draconis Combine's most prestigious combat regiments. As the initial Genyosha example, Dragonfly brought the Crow's electronic warfare and reconnaissance capabilities to a formation with an established history of operating the Combine's most advanced equipment. The aircraft operates in the standard reconnaissance configuration with full target designation, electronic suppression, and active probe capability. Its operational record within the Genyosha established an early positive precedent for the Crow's performance in elite Combine service.
text.capabilities: Dragonfly operates in the standard production Crow Scout Helicopter configuration, with no modifications from the production baseline. Speed, armor, and airframe construction are identical to other production aircraft. The Skyhunter IV targeting system with its Forward-1 TAG designator provides the aircraft's primary combat contribution through target designation for guided munitions, supported by the Wunderland Beagle Active Probe for target identification and tracking. The Scuti Dualcom communications system with its Apple-Churchill Guardian ECM suite provides electronic suppression capability. The Exostar extended-range small lasers provide backup direct engagement capability, though DCMS operational assessments consistently classify the Crow as a designation and reconnaissance platform rather than a primary combatant.
text.deployment: Dragonfly serves with the Genyosha in a forward reconnaissance and target designation role, operating in coordination with the regiment's BattleMech forces to provide electronic support and guided munitions designation. Its operational record within the Genyosha has contributed to broader DCMS confidence in the Crow as a high-value reconnaissance asset for elite formations.
text.battleHistory:
Dragonfly entered service with the Genyosha in 3070 as the regiment's first assigned Crow Scout Helicopter. Operating the standard reconnaissance configuration, the aircraft's crew quickly demonstrated effective employment of the TAG designation capability, accumulating four confirmed kills through coordinated guided munitions strikes. The performance record established early confidence in the Crow's value as a forward targeting asset, affirming Yan Manufacturing's claims for the design's operational effectiveness in elite Combine service.

The crew has been active in lobbying Genyosha technical staff for authorization to replace the Exostar small lasers with a C3 slave module, arguing that the aircraft's limited direct combat effectiveness makes the laser armament redundant weight, while a C3 slave would meaningfully enhance the crew's contribution to the regiment's integrated fire control network. The request reflects a broader operational assessment within DCMS that network integration may represent a more valuable capability trade for experienced Crow operators than direct engagement potential.

production.targeting: Skyhunter IV w/ C3 Slave and Wunderland Beagle Active Probe

text.overview: The Crow (C3) is a Draconis Combine-exclusive variant of the Crow Scout Helicopter, developed by Yan Manufacturing to address Forward-1 TAG equipment shortages during the early Jihad years. By substituting a C3 slave computer for the standard target designation system, the variant adapts the Crow for integration into lance-level command networks without altering the airframe's performance profile. The C3 configuration retains the full electronic warfare suite of the base reconnaissance model, making it a capable networked asset for DCMS formations organized around C3 master equipment. The variant entered service in 3070 and has not been made available through commercial channels.
text.capabilities: The C3 variant replaces the standard Forward-1 TAG designator with a C3 slave computer, integrating the aircraft into lance command networks without otherwise altering its technical profile. Maximum speed, armor protection, and airframe construction remain identical to the base reconnaissance model. The Exostar extended-range small lasers provide the same engagement capability, and the Scuti Dualcom communications system with its Apple-Churchill Guardian ECM suite continues to deliver electronic suppression. The Wunderland Beagle Active Probe retains full target acquisition functionality. The trade-off exchanges guided munitions designation capability for lance-wide sharing of targeting data, a substitution considered tactically favorable by DCMS commanders operating integrated C3 formations. Commanders note that the aircraft's speed advantage persists regardless of electronics configuration. All logistical characteristics, including the composite rotor blade supply dependency on New Samarkand, carry forward from the standard model without modification.
text.deployment: The C3 variant serves exclusively within Draconis Combine formations, assigned to units operating C3 master-equipped lances where its network contribution offsets the absence of TAG designation capability. Early production went to elite regiments including the Genyosha and the Ryuken, with subsequent distribution extending to regular DCMS line units as production output permitted. The variant is not available through commercial channels and has not been observed in non-Combine service.
text.battleHistory: Yan Manufacturing introduced the C3 configuration in response to intermittent supply constraints on Forward-1 TAG equipment during the Jihad period. Rather than allow production gaps in Crow output, Yan's engineers identified the C3 slave computer as a functionally compatible substitute requiring minimal airframe modification. The DCMS supported the substitution, finding the variant's ability to integrate with existing C3 master networks a practical advantage for formations already organized around network-centric doctrine. Yan produced the configuration across multiple production runs as supply conditions dictated, without establishing it as a dedicated parallel line. The variant entered service in 3070 alongside the broader entry of Crow production into wide DCMS distribution. Distribution remained exclusively within the Combine, consistent with standing policy restricting C3 equipment from commercial export. Reports from elite units fielding the variant have been positive, with network integration described as a meaningful upgrade for lances already equipped with C3 master systems.

text.overview: The Crow (Export) is a dedicated strike and harassment variant of the Crow Scout Helicopter, developed by Yan Manufacturing for the open mercenary market. Removing the standard model's advanced electronics package entirely and replacing it with conventional direct-fire weapons, Yan produced an attack aircraft priced at approximately one-third the cost of the reconnaissance version. The export Crow trades intelligence-gathering capability for direct combat effectiveness and affordability, making it accessible to mercenary commands that cannot justify the cost of the standard configuration. The variant entered commercial circulation in 3069 and has attracted consistent demand across Inner Sphere mercenary markets.
text.capabilities: The export Crow replaces the reconnaissance model's full electronics suite with a pair of machine guns and a bank of one-shot rocket launchers, trading electronic warfare capability for direct firepower and dramatically reduced cost. The DAV 100 fusion engine and composite rotor construction remain unchanged, preserving top speed as the variant's primary survivability mechanism. Armor protection is heavier than the standard reconnaissance model, reflecting the export version's role as an active combatant accepting closer engagement ranges. The machine guns provide reliable sustained harassment capability, while the rocket launchers offer a single concentrated strike against hardened targets. As with all Crow variants, non-Combine operators must source locally manufactured rotor blade substitutes when original equipment wears out, with the predictable reduction in performance under sustained operational stress.
text.deployment: The export Crow serves primarily with mercenary commands throughout the Inner Sphere, fulfilling strike, harassment, and screening roles across a wide range of operational environments. Its substantially lower cost makes the design accessible to smaller organizations that cannot afford the standard reconnaissance model, and the absence of restricted electronics allows unrestricted commercial sale outside the Draconis Combine. Demand has consistently exceeded initial production estimates, with multiple consecutive runs sold out in advance.
text.battleHistory: Yan Manufacturing developed the export variant concurrently with the standard DCMS model, anticipating that the reconnaissance version's premium electronics costs would price it beyond the budgets of most mercenary commands. Stripping the advanced sensor suite eliminated the greatest cost driver while producing a vehicle still capable of contributing to combined arms operations through direct firepower. The export version entered service in 3069, ahead of the standard reconnaissance model's broad DCMS distribution. Initial production runs sold out quickly among mercenary buyers, and the following three runs were committed before the design reached wide circulation. Despite lacking electronic warfare capability, mercenary commanders consistently valued the combination of the export Crow's exceptional speed with its conventional armament for harassment, screening, and light strike assignments. The variant's approximately one-third cost advantage over the standard model drove demand that persisted through the disruptions of the Jihad period.

text.overview: The Cyrano Gunship is a thirty-ton VTOL combat vehicle developed by Paulina Weapons of the Taurian Concordat in 2622. Conceived as a light escort gunship to accompany heavier strike aircraft, the Cyrano attracted immediate attention from the Star League Defense Force following its introduction, and the SLDF became the design's primary customer. Combining genuine speed, extended endurance, and a sophisticated targeting suite, the Cyrano represented a capable blend of intelligence-gathering and fire support in a single airframe. While pilots universally criticized its thin armor protection, maintenance crews prized its reliable systems and low servicing requirements. By the Golden Age of the Star League, virtually every army and division maintained at least three squadrons, cementing the Cyrano's position as a standard escort and patrol platform. Production disruptions in the third millennium interrupted the line for generations before a factory rebuilding in 3071 restored the design to active availability.
text.capabilities:
The Cyrano's DAV 220 fusion engine drives the thirty-ton airframe to a cruising speed of 130 kph and a flank speed near 200 kph, placing it among the fastest vehicles in its weight class. This velocity supports rapid repositioning, extended patrol endurance, and disengagement from threats that outgun it. Primary armament is a nose-mounted Fuersturm-C large laser fired by either pilot or navigator/cargo master, a configuration that provides fire capability even in the event of crew casualties.

The Sky Tracer WL targeting and tracking system, integrated with a Beagle Active Probe, gives the Cyrano substantial battlefield intelligence value beyond its direct combat contribution. The probe retains up to thirty minutes of footage for replay, enabling fire information officers to conduct detailed post-engagement analysis. Garret M250 communications equipment supports squadron coordination and ground force liaison.

Paulina DL ferro-fibrous armor provides protection somewhat better than standard plate for equivalent weight, but the total coverage remains thin for a vehicle regularly committed to escort and combat patrol missions. Pilots routinely cite the armor as the Cyrano's most significant tactical weakness, and experienced crews have learned to use the design's exceptional speed to compensate, avoiding situations where sustained fire can accumulate. Long fuel endurance and self-conforming pilot seats reduce crew fatigue on extended operations.
text.deployment:
During the Golden Age of the Star League, the Cyrano was a near-universal presence in SLDF escort and patrol formations, with most armies and divisions maintaining three or more full squadrons. Low maintenance requirements made it popular with logistics planners, while the Beagle Active Probe's footage replay capability drove demand for the design as a training and intelligence platform. Pilots accepted the thin armor as a professional inconvenience, relying on speed to minimize exposure rather than seeking sustained engagements.

Following the 3071 factory rebuilding, the Taurian Concordat's conventional infantry and armored divisions have become the Cyrano's primary operators, with the Protectorate Militia using it heavily as an escort and transport support vehicle. Persistent demand for the design exceeds available production, and units are rarely present in the numbers commanders prefer. The ML and Plasma variants address specific operational requirements, with the ML model serving open-market customers and the Plasma variant equipping TDF strike force escort elements.
text.battleHistory:
The Cyrano traces its origins to the economic opportunities created in the Taurian Concordat following the Reunification War. Paulina Weapons, originally a Tigress-based small-arms manufacturer, expanded operations after the Star League encouraged Periphery industry development as part of post-war reconstruction. The company established a substantial production complex near New Vandenberg's capital, employing over two thousand workers and helping revitalize the planet's war-damaged economy within two years. The SLDF became an immediate and enthusiastic customer when the Cyrano entered service in 2622, purchasing the gunship for escort and patrol duty across virtually every formation in the military.

Paulina engineers developed enhanced variants through the Star League era, including the Royal variant by 2721 for elite SLDF formations, and the experimental Fury variant beginning in 2754. Only six Fury prototypes were built for the SLDF's elite Fury Teams. All six were committed to combat on Terra during the liberation from Amaris's forces, tasked with a strike against a Reagan space defense facility. Active defenses destroyed the Fury Teams' infantry in the initial approach, forcing a conventional assault that cost all six Cyranos as well. None of the Fury prototypes survived the campaign.

The New Vandenberg production line operated through the Star League era until disruption ended production around 2840. For generations, popular history attributed the plant's destruction to a FedSuns-financed pirate force. Evidence emerging during the Jihad pointed instead to ComStar's Operation Holy Shroud, a revelation the Word of Blake leveraged politically in their offer to rebuild the facility at no cost to the Taurian people. The Word completed reconstruction, and new Cyranos lifted from the New Vandenberg line in late 3071. The Taurian Concordat is expected to assume full ownership of the facility in the coming decade.

text.overview: The Cyrano (ML) is an open-market variant of the Cyrano Gunship developed by Paulina Weapons at New Vandenberg in 3071 alongside the facility's reconstruction. Designed to serve customers outside the Taurian Defense Force, the ML model replaces the original large laser with a pair of Exostar medium lasers and a battery of rocket launcher pods, trading long-range punch for improved short-range firepower and broader logistical accessibility. The design retains the original DAV 220 fusion engine and most of the base Cyrano's systems, adding a modest armor improvement from weight saved by the lighter armament. Intended for escort, scout, and light patrol duties across a range of operational contexts, the ML variant has found buyers throughout the post-Jihad Inner Sphere who value the Cyrano platform's proven reliability and exceptional speed.
text.capabilities:
The Cyrano (ML) substitutes two Exostar medium lasers for the base model's Fuersturm-C large laser, accepting reduced range in exchange for a more heat-efficient armament with better short-range performance against lightly armored targets. Multiple rocket launcher pods add burst damage capacity, enabling effective engagement of infantry concentrations and lightly armored vehicles. The original DAV 220 fusion engine and Paulina DL ferro-fibrous armor are retained, with the ML carrying an additional half-ton of armor compared to the base model.

The Sky Tracer WL targeting and tracking system with Beagle Active Probe carries forward from the base design, preserving the intelligence-gathering capability that made the standard Cyrano attractive as a patrol platform. Garret M250 communications equipment remains unchanged. The ML's medium laser and rocket load make it effective in close escort and screening roles where the original large laser's extended range is less operationally relevant. Its greatest weakness mirrors the base model, as the ferro-fibrous armor, while improved over the original, still leaves the crew exposed to sustained fire from heavier opponents.
text.deployment: The Cyrano (ML) serves open-market customers across the Inner Sphere in escort, scout, and light patrol roles. Its accessible armament and the Cyrano platform's established logistical footprint make it attractive to smaller powers, mercenary units, and planetary militia organizations that lack the supply chains to support more exotic weapon systems. The short-to-medium range armament and rocket pods suit it for close escort duty alongside ground armor columns and for screening operations in terrain that limits long-range engagements. Taurian Concordat forces use limited numbers alongside the Plasma variant, and post-Jihad commerce has placed ML models in service across multiple successor states.
text.battleHistory:
The ML variant emerged directly from the Word of Blake's reconstruction of the Paulina Weapons facility at New Vandenberg in the early 3070s. While the Taurian Defense Force sought a platform tailored to their specific operational requirements, Paulina engineers recognized demand for a less specialized version capable of finding buyers on the open market. The decision to replace the Fuersturm large laser with the more widely available Exostar medium laser platform and add rocket launcher pods reflected both cost considerations and the need to appeal to customers who lacked access to TDF-specific logistics chains.

Production of the ML and Plasma variants began simultaneously at New Vandenberg in late 3071, with both designs shipping to their respective customers as the rebuilt factory reached full capacity. The ML quickly established a presence across the post-Jihad Inner Sphere as replacement stock for formations that had relied on older Cyrano chassis worn out during the conflicts of the prior decade.

text.overview: The Cyrano (Plasma) is a variant developed by Paulina Weapons in 3071 specifically for the Taurian Defense Force. Leveraging light engine technology obtained through trade with the Outworlds Alliance, the design retains the exceptional speed of the base Cyrano while freeing enough tonnage to substantially improve armor protection and mount a plasma rifle better suited to escort duty against sophisticated modern threats. The Plasma variant was intended to address TDF commanders' longstanding frustration with the original Cyrano's thin protection and limited effectiveness against current armor, replacing the base model's large laser with a weapon traded to the Concordat specifically to help defend against the Davion threat on the Taurian frontier.
text.capabilities:
The Cyrano (Plasma) employs a lighter fusion engine than the base model, made possible by technology shared with the Taurian Concordat through Outworlds Alliance trade. The engine swap retains the Cyrano's extraordinary speed while the saved tonnage is applied to two additional tons of Paulina DL ferro-fibrous armor, bringing total protection to a level commanders consider substantially more appropriate for an escort vehicle committed to contested airspace.

Primary armament is a plasma rifle from the Concordat's newer weapons inventory, replacing the Fuersturm-C large laser. The plasma rifle offers superior anti-armor penetration and a heat-inducing secondary effect that is especially useful for suppressing opposing aircraft and vehicles that rely on cooling efficiency. The Sky Tracer WL targeting system with Beagle Active Probe and Garret M250 communications carry forward from the base model unchanged, preserving the design's intelligence-gathering capabilities while adding dedicated strike-force firepower.
text.deployment: The Cyrano (Plasma) serves the Taurian Defense Force as an escort gunship for Nightshade and Ripper heavy strike formations, replacing earlier model Cyranos in TDF air wings. Its plasma rifle armament makes it effective against armored opposition encountered during contested strike operations, and the additional armor improves crew survivability in engagements that exceed the standard Cyrano's narrow defensive margins. Deployment is concentrated in Taurian Concordat formations, with limited quantities allocated to allied militia organizations in the Hyades Rim. Despite persistent demand, the Protectorate Militia's transport and escort requirements routinely outpace available Plasma variant supply.
text.battleHistory:
The Plasma variant's development is inseparable from the Taurian Concordat's security concerns in the early 3070s. Decades of Federated Suns pressure on the Taurian periphery had convinced TDF planners that the standard Cyrano's armament was insufficient against modern Davion air assets. The Outworlds Alliance's willingness to share plasma rifle technology as part of a broader diplomatic and trade arrangement gave Paulina engineers a weapon platform suited to address this requirement. Development proceeded concurrently with the New Vandenberg facility's reconstruction, and both the Plasma and ML variants entered production in late 3071.

The TDF's acceptance was immediate, and Protectorate Militia formations began transitioning from older Cyranos to the new model as production capacity allowed. The Blakist workers who staffed the rebuilt facility during its initial operational period provided technical continuity, though TDF and Paulina personnel moved steadily to assume full operational control over the following years.

text.overview: The Cyrano (Royal) is an enhanced Star League-era variant of the Cyrano Gunship manufactured by Paulina Weapons at their original Tigress headquarters. Developed to meet the higher performance standards required by elite SLDF formations and the Royal Brigades, the Royal variant incorporated upgraded Star League-grade systems throughout the airframe. First produced in 2721, it served alongside the standard Cyrano in SLDF inventories until the eventual loss of the Tigress production facility. Few examples survived the conflicts following the Star League's collapse, and the type has not been produced since the plant's destruction.
text.capabilities:
The Cyrano (Royal) builds on the standard model's capable foundation with Star League-grade components suited to the exacting standards of SLDF elite formations. The base Fuersturm-C large laser armament is retained, giving the Royal the same primary fire capability as the standard Cyrano at ranges that complement the escort mission profile. Paulina DL ferro-fibrous armor carries forward, with enhanced manufacturing tolerances producing tighter protection suited to elite formations' expectations.

The Sky Tracer WL targeting system with Beagle Active Probe operates with refined sensor calibration and improved data processing, supporting the intelligence review requirements of staff-level fire information officers. Garret M250 communications equipment supports coordinated operations across mixed-formation taskforces. The DAV 220 fusion engine provides the same exceptional speed as the standard model, with Royal-grade manufacturing producing reduced mechanical variance and improved reliability across extended operational deployments. As with the base Cyrano, the Royal's primary tactical limitation is armor coverage that experienced crews considered thin for the demands of escort duty against modern weapons.
text.deployment: The Cyrano (Royal) served exclusively within SLDF elite formations and Royal Brigades in escort and patrol roles requiring the highest available gunship capability. Its enhanced systems made it the preferred choice for staff-level air escort and intelligence-gathering missions where the Beagle Active Probe's performance was operationally critical. Outside the SLDF, the type saw limited distribution among a small number of high-capability Successor State forces that had received Star League surplus. As surviving examples diminished through Succession Wars attrition, the Royal was progressively replaced by the standard Cyrano or other escort types. No production has resumed following the loss of the Tigress facility.
text.battleHistory:
The Royal variant entered service with SLDF elite formations in 2721, nearly a century after the base Cyrano's introduction. Paulina Weapons developed the enhanced model from their original Tigress headquarters, applying the company's growing technical resources to meet Star League specifications for a premium-grade escort gunship. Royal Brigades and other elite formations used the type alongside the standard Cyrano through the remainder of the Star League era.

The Tigress facility continued production of both standard and Royal variants until the Star League's collapse. Following the Amaris Civil War and General Kerensky's Exodus, the Tigress plant passed first to independent operators and then to the Capellan Confederation as that state expanded into former Taurian and independent systems during the early Succession Wars. Production ceased with the plant's absorption into Capellan territory. Without the Tigress facility, the Royal variant could not be reproduced, and surviving examples were worn down through the brutal attrition of the Succession Wars. By the Late Succession Wars, the type had effectively vanished from active inventories, surviving only in deep storage or as museum pieces in a handful of Concordat and Capellan facilities.

text.overview: The Daimyo HQ is a heavy wheeled command vehicle designed and built by Buda Imperial Vehicles on Luthien for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Weighing twice as much as the standard Mobile HQ, the Daimyo was intended to provide theater-level command capability while offering substantially more defensive firepower than lighter command platforms. Conceived before the Succession Wars began, the Daimyo reflected the Combine's emphasis on powerful, self-sufficient command assets that could operate forward of the main logistics chain. Combine commanders received the vehicle with great enthusiasm, and it quickly became a fixture in DCMS line regiments during its initial production run.
text.capabilities:
The Daimyo's most distinctive feature is its expandable sides, which slide outward to reveal a mid-sized holotank and nearly double the available floor space, creating a full field command center within minutes. The vehicle can travel with its sides expanded but cannot exceed cruising speed in that configuration, as the off-center weight distribution risks damaging the chassis.

A Sipher Battlesys 5.2 computer feeds real-time data from the seven tons of communications equipment to the holotank, allowing commanders to manage everything from small DEST operations to orbital defense coordination. Eagle Eye VY 9-3 targeting tracking and the Sipher communications package together represent the most sophisticated electronics suite fitted to any Combine command vehicle of its era. A RAMTech 1200 large laser in the turret provides serious defensive firepower at range, while four Type 87 machine guns protect against infantry threats. StarSlab/3 armor and a four-ton infantry bay for security personnel complete the defensive package. The Vlar 230 fusion engine provides a cruising speed of 54 km/h.
text.deployment: The 67-NC strips all seven tons of communications equipment from the standard Daimyo in favor of a larger engine that boosts maximum speed to 96 km/h. The armament remains identical to the 67-K, but the infantry compartment is reduced to three tons. This variant serves as a fast escort and chase vehicle, designed to keep pace with retreating enemies or screen the slower command variants from flanking threats. It does not function as a command vehicle despite sharing the Daimyo chassis.
text.battleHistory:
In late 2796, the first production Daimyo HQs were issued to units on Kentares. The vehicle assigned to Coordinator Jinjiro Kurita himself became infamous during the Kentares Massacre. For the first two months of the atrocity, the Coordinator watched executions on the Daimyo's interior monitors. When he began attending them in person, the horrified crew passed recordings to a local ComStar representative, who broadcast the evidence across the Inner Sphere. The crew paid for their defiance with their lives.

Production continued through the early Succession Wars, with Daimyos found in every DCMS line regiment. As the wars ground on, the Sipher Battlesys computer became irreplaceable LosTech, and finding substitutes proved fruitless. The 67-K fell out of widespread use after the Fourth Succession War, and Buda closed the production line in 3027. After years of delay, new Daimyos began rolling off the line in 3063 in limited numbers, with priority going to front-line formations. The 67-K2 upgrade featured light PPCs in place of the original large laser, while the 67-R was developed under contract for the Free Rasalhague Republic's KungsArme, mounting a plasma cannon and rocket launchers. A small number of 67-NC chase variants stripped all communications equipment for a larger engine, serving as fast escort vehicles for the command variants they were designed to protect.

text.overview: The Danai Support Vehicle is a forty-five-ton wheeled artillery platform produced by Detroit Consolidated Vehicle Works on Detroit, entering service in 3073 through a joint initiative between the Magistracy of Canopus and the Capellan Confederation under the terms of the Trinity Alliance. Named for Danai Centrella, the fallen heir to the Canopian throne, the design was commissioned to provide the Magistracy Armed Forces with a mobile indirect fire support platform capable of operating across the combined-arms formations that the alliance required. Although the construction of Capellan-funded factories on a Magistracy world generated political friction within Canopian circles, the vehicle that emerged proved capable enough to win acceptance in both Canopian and Capellan formations. Its balance of speed, durability, and long-range fire support has made the Danai a reliable fixture in combined-arms units, and commanders on both sides of the alliance have come to depend on its steady performance.
text.capabilities:
The Danai's primary weapon is a Bithinian Ballistics Thumper artillery piece mounted in a fixed forward position on the hull rather than a rotating turret. This arrangement restricts the direct engagement arc but reduces mechanical complexity and frees mass for propulsion, protection, and secondary armament. Two Firmir Improved Extended-Range Medium Lasers occupy the turret, providing a credible self-defense reach against vehicles and infantry that close with the artillery platform, extending coverage well beyond what standard medium lasers would allow. A GM 205 fusion engine delivers a flank speed of 86 kilometers per hour, permitting rapid displacement between fire positions and timely withdrawal ahead of opposing counter-battery responses.

Six and a half tons of Maximillian 43 armor provides adequate protection for a vehicle not intended for direct combat. The Magestrix Alpha communications system and Magestrix Gamma targeting suite are standard Magistracy vehicle electronics, simplifying field maintenance and supply across the MAF's mixed vehicle inventory. The Danai's most significant tactical constraint is its fixed gun mount, which requires the entire vehicle to reorient for targets outside the forward arc, but its speed and self-defense weapons give it survivability that many comparable artillery platforms cannot match.
text.deployment: The Danai entered continuous production in 3073 and has spread to nearly every Canopian combat unit and many Capellan formations. The MAF employs it primarily in indirect fire support roles, pairing the vehicle with faster screening elements that provide close protection while the artillery platform engages targets beyond direct-fire range. Mercenary units under Canopian and Capellan contract have consistently sought access to the type. While early MAF policy restricted sales to state-sponsored units, subsequent policy changes opened the market to mercenary purchasers. The factory security force at Detroit has historically maintained two full companies of Danais as its primary defensive asset, a practice that proved its worth during the Word of Blake raid on the facility.
text.battleHistory:
The Danai's origins lie in the political arrangements that followed the Trinity Alliance. While the Capellans had provided significant educational and economic assistance to the Magistracy, the construction of Capellan-funded manufacturing facilities on Detroit, a Magistracy world, generated resentment in Canopian political circles. To offer Canopians a tangible military benefit from the arrangement, Capellan planners collaborated with the MAF to design a new artillery support vehicle for Canopian service. Two hundred Bithinian Ballistics Thumper artillery pieces were shipped from Capellan suppliers to Detroit under heavy guard to ensure a consistent initial production run, and the first vehicles entered service in 3073.

The design was named for Danai Centrella, the late heir to the Canopian throne, as a gesture of respect to Canopian sentiment. Its introduction coincided with a period of intense operational demand as the Jihad spread conflict throughout the Periphery and Confederation, and the new vehicle quickly spread into MAF combat formations and many Capellan units. The largest single concentration of Danais remained the factory security force at Detroit itself, where two full companies guarded the production complex.

In 3073 a surprise Word of Blake raiding force struck the Detroit facilities before the defenders could organize an adequate response. Commander Erin Bowker, the senior Danai commander in the security battalions, improvised a solution under fire. Ordering MAF BattleMechs to slow the advancing Blakists, Bowker maneuvered all available Danais away from the raiders and into a firing position covering the Blakist Seeker-class DropShip on the ground. A sustained time-on-target artillery barrage prevented the ship from lifting, and when the MAF lance closed in, the stranded raiding force was trapped between 'Mech and Danai fire. The action demonstrated both the vehicle's tactical flexibility and the lethality of its artillery at extended range.

Production at Detroit continued through the post-Jihad period. As the Capellan Confederation's political and economic grip on the Canopian orbit tightened during the Dark Age, the Detroit facility transitioned to Capellan administration, and the Danai remained in active production into the ilClan era under Capellan management.

text.overview: The Danai Arrow is an experimental prototype refit developed by Detroit Consolidated Vehicle Works beginning in 3075 under the direction of R&D manager Sagira Tabatabai. The project began as a salvage effort following the Word of Blake raid on Detroit, which left a large number of factory-fresh Danais heavily damaged before they could enter service. What started as a program to recover functional vehicles from the wreckage evolved into a systematic prototype design effort. Substituting an Arrow IV artillery system for the Danai's standard Thumper and replacing the turret lasers with Magshot Gauss rifles, the Arrow configuration trades operational support range for the more flexible deployment options enabled by the Arrow IV's specialized munitions. A subsequent upgrade phase added vehicular stealth armor, introducing integration complications that have so far prevented the design from advancing beyond experimental status.
text.capabilities:
The Arrow replaces the standard Danai's Bithinian Ballistics Thumper with an Arrow IV artillery launcher mounted in the forward hull position, reducing operational support range in exchange for access to the broader munitions library available for the Arrow IV system, including homing rounds compatible with ground-based target designators. Four Magshot Gauss rifles in the turret replace the Firmir extended-range lasers, providing reliable kinetic fire against conventional and armored infantry targets. A Guardian ECM suite, added during the second prototype phase, occupies body space and required installation of a smaller DAV 160-rated fusion engine to manage the vehicle's weight and internal volume requirements, reducing flank speed by more than twenty kilometers per hour compared to the standard Danai.

Seven tons of vehicular stealth armor, adapted from Hellespont Stealth plate originally developed for BattleMech applications, provides a half-ton more protection than the standard Danai configuration while reducing the vehicle's electromagnetic signature. The integration of this armor and the Guardian with the inherited Magestrix Gamma targeting system has proved problematic: the targeting suite lacks hardening against the Guardian's ECM field, generating faulty fire control data, intermittently failing to relay launch commands to the Arrow IV, and occasionally shutting down entirely. DCVW has restricted the Arrow's deployment to dire circumstances only until a solution is found.
text.deployment: No Danai Arrows have entered general service. Only four prototypes were constructed during the initial Arrow IV phase, and three surviving units were subsequently converted to the stealth armor configuration. These three vehicles remain at Detroit Consolidated Vehicle Works under restricted evaluation status, authorized for combat deployment only in extreme circumstances due to the unresolved targeting system incompatibility with the Guardian ECM suite. Interested parties may contact DCVW account managers regarding program investment, with a minimum threshold of five million C-Bills. Whether the Arrow progresses to limited production depends entirely on whether funding and a technical solution arrive before the prototypes are scrapped.
text.battleHistory:
The Word of Blake raid on Detroit in 3073 left a substantial number of factory-fresh Danai Support Vehicles severely damaged in the facility crossfire. DCVW engineers initially attempted to cobble together functional vehicles from the salvaged components, but the scale of usable material led R&D manager Sagira Tabatabai to propose a more deliberate redesign. Replacing the Thumper with an Arrow IV launcher and the Firmir lasers with Magshot Gauss rifles, the first prototype phase produced four test vehicles. These early Arrow IV prototypes demonstrated viable tactical performance, offering a more flexible indirect fire option than the base Danai's fixed Thumper.

A year into the program, a parts shortage halted production of the Anubis, prompting Tabatabai's team to attempt adapting that 'Mech's Hellespont Stealth armor for vehicular use. The three surviving Arrow IV prototypes were stripped and rebuilt with a smaller DAV 160-rated engine to accommodate the stealth system and Guardian ECM suite. The revised configuration added half a ton of armor protection over the original Arrow prototypes at the cost of significant speed reduction.

The retrofit introduced serious complications. The Magestrix Gamma targeting system proved incompatible with the Guardian's ECM field, intermittently producing faulty data, failing to issue launch commands to the missile system, and occasionally shutting down entirely, leaving the vehicle defenseless during reboots. DCVW restricted all three surviving Arrow prototypes to emergency deployment and continued live-fire trials seeking a fix. As of 3076, the program is steadily losing funding as other DCVW initiatives advance, and the minimum outside investment to continue development stands at five million C-Bills. All three prototypes face the prospect of scrapping if a solution and a sponsor do not materialize.

text.deployment: The standard Darter fills conventional reconnaissance and screening roles across Federated Suns conventional forces and allied units. Its three tons of flexible cargo allow crews to tailor the vehicle to specific mission needs, from communications equipment to supplies to additional personnel. The design sees its widest deployment with combined-arms formations where its speed and minimal logistical burden make it an acceptable risk for forward scouting ahead of heavier assets.

This configuration sacrifices half the standard Darter's cargo capacity to mount a Beagle active probe, giving the crew active sensor capability for detecting concealed units at short range. The BAP variant is deployed with combined-arms units operating in environments where passive scouting is likely to miss entrenched infantry or hidden equipment. The trade of cargo utility for detection capability makes it most valuable in close terrain where sensor intelligence is worth more than general logistical flexibility.

The C3 variant replaces one ton of cargo with a C3 slave unit, allowing the vehicle to feed targeting data to friendly units equipped with compatible master computers. The Darter's speed and small profile make it well suited to operating as a forward observer within organized C3 networks, extending effective engagement ranges for fire support elements by providing frontline targeting data from positions too exposed for heavier platforms.
text.battleHistory:
The Darter came into being as a product of post-First Succession War necessity. The conflict had devastated Federated Suns conventional forces, and with reconstruction almost entirely focused on BattleMech production, the AFFS faced chronic shortages of light reconnaissance assets. Facing pressure to fill support roles without consuming fusion engines or advanced components, the AFFS solicited proposals from multiple manufacturers. General Motors' Kathil proposal, a vehicle constructible from locally sourced materials and maintainable without specialized tools, won the production contract in 2822.

The design's first significant test came in June 2828, during the opening campaigns of the Second Succession War. Capellan Confederation forces landed on Orbisonia in force, the invasion championed by heavy BattleMechs that threatened to overwhelm the outnumbered Davion defenders. A company of Darters deployed in the region transformed what appeared to be a hopeless defense. Moving too quickly for the Confederation's heavier machines to close with, the vehicles fed continuous intelligence to Davion Hussar regiments, allowing the AFFS to exploit gaps in the Capellan advance with precision. On the fourth day, one of the Darters identified Chancellor Ilsa Liao leading the rear-guard action. The information enabled a Federated Suns strike that cut the Chancellor's withdrawal route. When Liao was killed during the subsequent fighting, the Capellan offensive collapsed entirely. The engagement made the Darter's operational debut one of the more consequential reconnaissance actions of the early Succession Wars, and stories of the action spread through conventional force circles for generations.

General Motors twice temporarily suspended Darter production to redirect Kathil's facility capacity: once in 3003 and again in 3037. Both suspensions were brief. The vehicle's low cost and continuing demand from conventional force commanders made permanent cancellation economically untenable, and the lines restarted both times without significant interruption to availability in the field. As advanced electronics became more accessible following the Helm Memory Core discovery, crews began adapting their vehicles with active probe systems, C3 slave hardware, electronic countermeasure suites, and light missile launchers. These field-origin configurations became sufficiently common that General Motors eventually cataloged them as recognized variants, even though the manufacturer does not officially offer them from the factory floor. The Darter's reputation for surviving on duct tape and salvaged parts remains as accurate in the ilClan era as it was the day the design first entered service.

text.deployment: Mounting a Guardian ECM suite in place of the Beagle probe, this variant provides electronic warfare support for units operating in sensor-dense environments. Its small signature and high speed allow it to shadow friendly formations while degrading enemy targeting and communications, fulfilling a disruption role without requiring a dedicated combat platform. The ECM variant sees common use in combined-arms actions where suppressing enemy sensors is prioritized over active reconnaissance.
