text.deployment: The standard Fulcrum was deployed primarily as a reconnaissance and fast-strike platform, concentrated along the Lyran Alliance's Periphery and Free Worlds League borders during its early production years. Its combination of speed, ECM, and TAG made it a natural fit for combined-arms formations requiring a mobile spotter and electronic screen. Following the FedCom Civil War, expanded production met demand from both Lyran and Federated Suns commands, with units appearing in light cavalry and scout lance roles throughout the Inner Sphere. Crews valued the vehicle's ease of repair in field conditions, which extended operational availability during campaigns far from major supply depots.

Production of the Fulcrum Hybrid at Johnston Industries' Benet III facility was constrained by the challenges of sourcing Clan-specification medium pulse lasers, resulting in smaller deliveries with longer lead times than standard production variants. Vehicles that reached front-line units were allocated primarily to Federated Suns Davion Light Combat Teams, where the Hybrid's brawling capability and electronic warfare suite complemented the Light Combat Team doctrine of rapid insertion and disruption. Its armored motive system and supercharger allowed the Hybrid to survive engagements that would destroy a standard Fulcrum, making it a preferred asset for high-risk penetration missions.

The Fulcrum II was introduced in 3067 to address demand for a variant better suited to urban and close-quarters combat. Replacing the large laser with additional medium lasers and a short-range missile rack trades long engagement reach for volume of fire at closer ranges. The variant served primarily in assault and exploitation roles within Lyran Alliance commands, complementing the standard model's reconnaissance focus. It was particularly effective when paired with standard Fulcrums, moving in to press engagements that the base model's firepower had opened.

text.deployment: The Fulcrum III refit kit, offered by Alphard Trading Corporation from the Dark Age onward, provided an upgrade path for operators seeking improved firepower and survivability without replacing the chassis. Replacing the original weapons with a Snub-Nose PPC and MML 7 broadens the engagement envelope, while a C3 slave unit integrates the Fulcrum into networked fire control arrangements. The heavy ferro-fibrous armor upgrade addresses the vehicle's longstanding vulnerability in sustained engagements. Distribution was primarily through Alphard Trading's commercial networks, with the kit seeing adoption by formations in the rimward Periphery where resupply from Inner Sphere manufacturers was inconsistent.

Only eight to ten Fulcrum X prototypes were confirmed produced, constructed within Armed Forces of the Federated Suns repair facilities at Gerard Barracks on New Syrtis beginning in 3075. One platoon served on loan to Duchess Hasek's forces in the Capellan March during the Jihad. The experimental systems, including reactive armor, an Angel ECM suite, and Clan-specification lasers, placed the design beyond standard logistics support, limiting its appeal to specialized units capable of sourcing and maintaining non-standard components. Despite impressive performance, the Fulcrum X remained a proof-of-concept that never advanced to serial production.

Reintroduced by JKAW following the rebuild of the design, this version entered service with Davion Assault Guards and other AFFS heavy armor formations. It performs the same command vehicle role as the original, coordinating armor and infantry operations from the second echelon. JKAW has sold this variant exclusively to AFFS commands, declining all outside offers. The design carries an infantry bay capable of transporting a single squad for close protection of the command crew.

The C3 Master variant pairs with up to three C3 Slave Furys to coordinate networked fire across a combined arms lance. Its plasma rifle and rotary autocannon provide effective close and medium range fire support while the master computer directs targeting solutions for its slave units. The expanded infantry bay accommodates either two squads of standard infantry or a single battle armor unit to screen the command vehicle from infantry threats.

Developed by JKAW during the Jihad to integrate the Fury into Federated Suns C3 network doctrine, the C3 Slave variant operates in combined lance formations alongside the C3 Master version. It feeds targeting data into the shared network while contributing its own Gauss and light autocannon fire. The light fusion engine and ferro-fibrous armor provide improved battlefield survivability compared to the standard Fury, at the cost of the infantry transport bay.

The production variant made available to Great House militaries and SLDF regular formations, the Fury II replaced the restricted Nirasaki-400X with a forward-facing medium laser and marginally increased side armor. It served across all major Inner Sphere powers during the late Star League period, valued for its long-range Gauss capability even without the advanced computer. All known operational examples were eventually destroyed or cannibalized for components during the Succession Wars.

The Fury III represents JKAW's Dark Age evolution of the design, incorporating an XL fusion engine and a Clan-built rotary autocannon alongside the retained Gauss rifle. Two ER medium lasers extend fire coverage across the front arc while C3 boosted slave equipment allows coordination with widely dispersed units. A Beagle active probe adds battlefield awareness suited to the fragmented engagements common in the Dark Age. The infantry bay has been removed to free tonnage for the expanded weapons and electronics suite.

The command master version of the Fury III exchanges the boosted C3 slave, active probe, and one ER medium laser for a C3 boosted master computer and a modest reduction in armor, allowing it to direct fire coordination for an entire network of linked vehicles. It operates as the tactical hub for formations equipped with Fury IIIs and compatible C3-networked units, retaining the Gauss rifle and Clan rotary autocannon for direct engagement capability.
